observations:
Torah LM2/24 contains only 2 bechina edges, yielding one merged package after analysis. All bechina-language in the source text has been accounted for within Package 1 plus one gap-analysis addition.

Search for independent domains with 3+ bechina-linked nodes:

1. The Simcha / Melody / Healing cluster: The Rebbe discusses שמחה, יוד מיני נגינה, תקון החולה, and ריקודין. All of these are explicitly equated through bechina language in the text and belong to Package 1. This is not an independent new domain — it IS Package 1 (enriched by the gap addition of יוד מיני נגינה).

2. The Pulse / Illness cluster: The Rebbe mentions 'יוד מיני דפיקין' (ten pulse types) and 'כל מיני חולאת' (all types of illness). However, the relationship between the ten melodies and the ten pulses is stated causally: 'אֵלּוּ יוּד מִינֵי נְגִינָה בָּאִין בְּתוֹךְ עֲשָׂרָה מִינֵי דְּפִיקִין, וְהֵם מְחַיִּין אוֹתָן' — the melodies ENTER INTO and ANIMATE the pulses. This is eitza (cause-and-effect flow), not bechina. No bechina language is used for this relationship. Furthermore, only one concept appears here; 'יוד מיני דפיקין' has no second bechina partner in the text, so it cannot form a package of 3+.

3. The Sadness / Illness cluster: 'מרה שחרה' (melancholy) and 'עצבות' (sadness) are presented as the source of illness and the opponent of simcha. These appear as causal agents: 'כָּל הַחוֹלַאַת הַבָּאִין עַל הָאָדָם, כֻּלָּם בָּאִין רַק מִקִּלְקוּל הַשִּׂמְחָה' and 'כָּל הַחוֹלַאַת – עַל־יְדֵי מָרָה שְׁחֹרָה וְעַצְבוּת'. The Rebbe never says 'מרה שחרה הוא בחינת X'. These concepts function as eitza causes (melancholy causes illness), not bechina pairs. No bechina cluster of 3+ evil concepts is formed.

4. Evil mirror consideration: The natural evil mirror of Package 1 (simcha as healing) would be 'מרה שחרה' (melancholy as illness). However, since the text does not use bechina language for the evil side, there is no basis for an evil package with bechina edges. The evil counterpart exists structurally in the teaching but not in the bechina graph.

5. The 'לב נשבר' (broken heart) concept in the second half of the text (lines 9-10) is presented in contrast to simcha, but with an eitza relationship: a broken heart can LEAD TO melancholy, not that it IS melancholy. The Rebbe distinguishes them carefully and recommends dedicating a specific time for broken-heartedness while maintaining simcha the rest of the day. No bechina equation is formed.

Conclusion: The single Package 1 fully covers the Torah's bechina structure. This Torah is a short, pithy teaching whose entire bechina content revolves around one central insight — simcha and dancing ARE the healing of illness — expressed through 2 bechina edges and enriched by one gap addition (יוד מיני נגינה). No independent new domain of 3+ bechina-connected concepts exists outside this package.
